introduction: “O God, my God! Thou seest me, Thou knowest me; Thou art my Haven and my Refuge.” This guide is a hundred prayers for nearness: thanks for having been drawn, counsel to turn to God at dawn and persevere in supplication, the lover’s language of thirst, fire and separation, the wish to want only what God wills, and many short petitions for whatever “will draw me nigh unto Thee”. The Psalms are the closest company, the hart panting for the water brooks, the soul that “longeth for the courts of the Lord”, “how long wilt thou hide thy face?”, “I had rather be a doorkeeper”. With them stand the Song of Songs, Augustine’s restless heart, Rumi’s reed lamenting its banishment, Rábi‘a, and the sayings that God is the one who comes: the Qur’an’s “surely I am nigh”, “I go to him running”, the father who ran. Tagore, who found freedom “in a thousand bonds of delight”, and Kabir’s “Lo! I am beside thee” question the picture of distance that the prayers take as their starting point.
questions: These prayers assume a distance to be crossed. The Qur’an says “surely I am nigh” and Kabir “I am beside thee”. What, then, is the distance, and whose is it?
Reading 33 advises turning to God “at the break of every morn”. What does regular practice add to longing, and what does longing add to practice?
The prayers of stretch three speak of thirst, fire and separation. Is this the language of a few ardent souls, or can an ordinary believer use it honestly?
“Whose only wish is what Thou hast determined.” How does wanting God’s will relate to wanting God’s nearness? Compare Dante’s “and his will is our peace”.
Tagore finds God in “a thousand bonds of delight”, not in renunciation. Would the authors of these prayers disagree?
Choose one short prayer from the last stretch. What would it mean, in a week’s ordinary events, for it to be answered?

outside.why: “Thou seest me, Thou knowest me; Thou art my Haven and my Refuge.” O Lord, thou hast searched me, and known me. Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising.
“None have I sought nor any will I seek save Thee.” Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.
“Leave not this servant to himself.” Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.
“Draw me nigh unto Thee.” Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.
The Qur’an’s assurance to every such prayer: when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me.
Birds with broken wings, thirsty fish. As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
“Make me as one of the fish in the ocean of Thy oneness.” In him we live, and move, and have our being.
Let my remoteness from home be a means of good. They confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
Grace has embraced me and bounty sustained me. Tagore: thy infinite gifts come to me only on these very small hands of mine. Ages pass, and still thou pourest, and still there is room to fill.
“Thy call hath attracted me.” Rumi’s poem opens with a call heard from far off: hearken to the reed-flute, how it complains, lamenting its banishment from its home.
Praise for having been guided. Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand. Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel.
At the break of every morn, set thy face toward the Kingdom. My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
Turn and supplicate fervently. Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.
Persevere in the station of supplication and utter weakness. A widow who wore down a judge by her continual coming; the parable is told to the end that men ought always to pray, and not to faint.
Fix thy gaze on the Most Exalted Horizon. I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
Standing before the door, turned to the lights of Thy face. As the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, so our eyes wait upon the Lord our God.
When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, Lord, will I seek.
“O Thou Whose nearness is my wish, Whose presence is my hope.” Augustine: You have made us for Yourself, and our hearts are restless until they rest in You.
Trials are a salve to those devoted to Thy will. Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.
“The ecstasy of my soul, the exultation of my heart.” In thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
The heart’s desire is presence at the Threshold. A day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God.
In separation they have rent their collars. By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
“How long shall this deprivation last?” How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
No quenching for my thirst but in the desert of Thy love. My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is.
My thirst entitles me to the stream of Thy presence. Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters.
The sighing of those who long to behold Thy face and are far. My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the Lord: my heart and my flesh crieth out for the living God.

Enkindled with the fire of separation. Tagore refuses the language of exile: deliverance is not for me in renunciation. I feel the embrace of freedom in a thousand bonds of delight. Must nearness to God be imagined as elsewhere, and this life as separation?
“Whose only wish is what Thou hast determined.” Not my will, but thine, be done.
One who sought only the good pleasure of Thy will. Dante hears it from a soul in Paradise: and his will is our peace.
Preserve me from all that would remove me from Thy nearness. He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit.
Purify us from the world and its conditions. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.
Rend asunder the veils that shut me out. Moses asked to see, and was answered: thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live. What would it mean for such a prayer to be granted?
Let not the vicissitudes of the world prevent me from drawing nigh. Neither death, nor life, nor things present, nor things to come, shall be able to separate us from the love of God.
“Place the world beneath thy feet.” I count all things but loss.
Oppressed among the wayward and a stranger. How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?
Make me one whom neither hardship nor ease keeps back. Paul’s list: in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in weariness and painfulness, in hunger and thirst.

“Graciously enable me to ascend unto Thee.” Paul: I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you. How do these prayers hold the wish to be with God together with work still to do here?
Poor, immerse me in Thy wealth; athirst, let me drink. Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
Suffer me not to be far from the court of Thy holiness. Cast me not away from thy presence; restore unto me the joy of thy salvation.
Deny me not the fragrances of Thy raiment in Thy days. My beloved is mine, and I am his.
“Cause me to soar in the atmosphere of Thy nearness.” They shall mount up with wings as eagles.
Grant us a shelter in Thy threshold. He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
An abode in the neighbourhood of Thy mercy. If a man love me, my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.
“Cast me not from Thy presence.” When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and ran.
“We have forsaken our homes, O Lord, in our eagerness to meet Thee.” Peter: behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee.
Open to their faces the gates of Thy grace. Knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
“I sense the fragrance of Thy manifestation but know not which place is illumined.” Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat!
Thy remoteness and separation have destroyed me. My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me?
“I know not whether Thy grace will bring me nigh.” Ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.
A handmaid who has desired nearness and reunion. Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
The reward of those who attained Thy presence, for one who could not. Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. Today shalt thou be with me in paradise.
That she may be carried wholly away from herself. Thomas à Kempis: love is a great thing; by itself it makes everything that is heavy, light.
Thirsty and homeless, and Thy court the asylum. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Gladden this sorrowing servant. Ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
Let these wanderers become Thy lovers, freed from the known and the unknown. Rábi‘a: Thou art enough for me.
Draw them nearer to the scene of Thy glory. Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory.
Ordain what will draw me nigh in all conditions. If he comes one span nearer to Me, I go one cubit nearer to him; and if he comes to Me walking, I go to him running.
Let me abide for ever before Thy countenance. I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.
That which will be with me in every world of Thy worlds. Whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge.
By Him Who conversed with the Tree. The bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.

A hundred prayers to be brought near. Kabir has the answer come from very close: O servant, where dost thou seek Me? Lo! I am beside thee. If that is so, what is all this asking for? What do the prayers themselves say about who is far from whom?

shortfall: The prayers of stretches four to seven and ten are petitions in a single form, each asking by a different Name for what will “draw me nigh unto Thee”; companions were set where a prayer adds an image or a turn of its own, and the remainder were left to their neighbours’.

psalm-continually-with-thee.text: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand. Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory

matthew-we-have-forsaken-all.text: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore
